target_customer: Local and state government records offices handling FOIA and public records requests
problem: Clerks spend hours searching for responsive records and redacting by hand while request volume grows and missed deadlines can bring lawsuits.
business_model: B2B SaaS sold to government agencies
product_category: GovTech AI agents for public records and FOIA

founders.name: Aditya Sabharwal
founders.background_notes: Some listings give him the CTO title; the YC page says CEO.

founders.name: Gleb Hulting
founders.background_notes: YC page says he bootstrapped EGO Logistics at 19 and won government contracts while in school.

competitors.name: GovQA
competitors.what: Public records request platform with AI assisted redaction
competitors.traction_then: challenger platform for high volume agencies

competitors.name: CivicPlus NextRequest
competitors.what: FOIA request portal with RapidReview redaction

competitors.name: Relativity FOIA
competitors.what: Purpose built FOIA software for agencies

technical_complexity.rationale: Search across email and shared drives, exemption aware redaction and audit trails need careful engineering and security (SOC 2 in preparation).

defensibility.rationale: Incumbent request trackers already hold customers and add AI features; integrations and compliance work create some stickiness.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents were adding AI redaction in 2026; no action against GovGuard found.

market_need_then: Founders say request volume grows about 2x a year without added staff and cities face suits for missed deadlines (YC launch post).

identity.logo: A logo mark on the site; details not found
identity.visual_style: Civic, institutional imagery of courthouses, town halls and stone textures with numbered sections
identity.voice_and_tone: Formal and trust oriented, security and compliance claims

brand_strength.rationale: Name signals government trust but similar names (GeoGuard, VoterGuard) exist and no brand press was found.

outcome_analysis: GovGuard is active in the Spring 2026 batch with a three person team and founders who previously sold public sector AI. Government sales cycles are slow and incumbents hold relationships, so the outcome is open; funding is not publicly verified.
notes: Stanford CodeX TechIndex lists total funding of 500K without investors or round; single source, so unverified and not recorded as a round. Founder education comes from the YC page. Competitor entries come from 2026 pages and are present day descriptions rather than dated at founding.
